name: グルテンフリーワッフル チャッフルズ 浅草
why: A chaffle is by definition a cheese-and-egg batter (「チーズや卵などを使って作る低糖質ワッフル」), and all five menu items carry cheese, egg, chicken or bacon. Tabelog's feature list says 「ベジタリアンメニューあり」 — vegetarian, never vegan, and the record's own vegan_detail concedes no confirmed plant-based item was found. 'Limited vegan options' overstates the evidence. Moot if the record is delisted as closed.

name: ベジタリアンカレー ナマステ
why: Both cited Roppongi vegan/vegetarian directories enumerate their venues in full and neither contains this name, and an exact-phrase search finds no such business. 'options' asserts a verified plant-based offering that no source supports; 'ask' is the highest tier the evidence carries.

name: からし亭
why: The only business the name resolves to is 焼肉 からし亭, an A5-beef yakiniku chain whose complete five-branch list contains no Minato-ku site. Nothing plant-based is offered by the brand, so 'ask' still invites a vegan diner to try. If instead the pin is an unrelated unlisted shop, the record should be withdrawn rather than re-tiered.

name: 個室ダイニング 門 赤坂
why: The only 門 any cited source documents is 和食処 門 (永田町), whose entire recorded menu is bonito / shrimp / clam / egg / butter, and the cited Akasaka 'washoku with vegetarian menu' list contains exactly two venues — 赤坂 花むら and 春秋 溜池山王店 — neither of them 門. Nothing supports even an 'ask'.

name: グリーンハウス
why: The record is filed under category VEGAN and renders the badge 'Fully vegan', but the operator is a general contract caterer whose consumer brands include とんかつ新宿さぼてん. Nothing indicates a vegan offer; 'ask' overstates it and the rendered label badly overstates it.

name: 蕎麦処 喜久や
why: A 蕎麦処 is filed under category VEGAN and renders the badge 'Fully vegan'. Even taking the record own text at face value, it says the tsuyu is almost certainly bonito- or sardine-based. The label contradicts the record own detail — exactly the defect class the brief names. If the record survives at all, vegan should read 'no'.

name: GLUTEN FREE CAFE avan エキュート上野
why: avan's own Q&A states dairy is in the base product, not just the toppings: 「チュロには、卵は使用しておりませんが、乳は使用しております。ただし、フレーバーによって、トッピングの材料に卵を使用している場合もございます。」 The Ueno store was built around 生クリーム (PR TIMES: 「エキュート上野店では生クリームを使用した、揚げたての米粉チュロ商品を中心にご用意します！」). Every churro on the menu therefore contains milk, and no plant-milk or vegan item is named anywhere. "Limited vegan options" implies something a vegan can eat; nothing here qualifies. Downgrade to "no". (Moot in practice — see the record verdict — but the label is wrong as it stands.)

name: 銀座 長寿庵
why: This is not an unknown. The operator states that every dipping sauce and broth in the house is built on 鰹節・宗田鰹節・鯖節 dashi, including the もり汁 and ざる汁 served with plain cold soba, so even the 精進天麩羅そば is not vegan. "ask" invites a vegan to ask a question the shop has already answered in public. Downgrade to "no", and fix vegan_label, which currently reads "Fully vegan".

name: Sakura Cafe Jimbocho
why: Every plant-forward item this venue publishes is labelled ベジタリアン, never ヴィーガン: ベジタリアンカレー and ファラフェルサンド carry no dairy/egg disclosure, and the dessert/drink line is dairy- and honey-heavy (マタルパニール cottage cheese, 青玉プリン made of egg+milk+honey, プティン). No source in Japanese or English uses the word vegan for this branch, so 'options' asserts a confirmed vegan path that no publisher has confirmed.
